- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75.00), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward bias correction for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates, model underestimates downside risk — increase downward drift or add volatility buffer.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if price is trending upward, forecast often flattens too early; adjust for momentum decay.
- When sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.33) and supply net is negative, model underestimates price drop — add 2–3% downward adjustment to forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate volatility in bearish regimes — increase standard deviation or add 1–2% downward bias in low-sentiment periods.
- If multiple auction events occur in 7–14 days, model overreacts to early events — delay forecast adjustment until 3–5 days after last event.
